Thanks Damian — got the diagram and IP allocation. Scheduling: Tue 2027-12-07 09:30 PT works for our ops/infra team. Invited.

High-level notes before the call so we can be efficient:
- Control plane (management, rollouts, health checks): we prefer a small set of customer-initiated TLS endpoints to the Redwood control plane on fixed ports (443 and 8443 for internal admin APIs). Those should be allowed from your VPC to our control-plane egress IPs. We’ll provide a CIDR block for the final phase.
- Data plane (inference traffic): two supported patterns depending on your preference:
  * Dedicated proxy in your VPC (recommended for strict egress control): a lightweight proxy VM or managed NAT that we run with an agent. All inference traffic exits your VPC as your IPs — simplifies compliance and logging.
  * Co-located sidecar/proxy (recommended for performance): a sidecar proxy in the same subnet as inference nodes that performs TLS termination for KV cache streaming and request batching; egress originates from sidecar ip range managed in your allocation.
- MTU: We support 1500 and jumbo (9000). If you use jumbo frames, ensure the overlay path to our control plane/peers preserves MTU; otherwise we recommend MSS clamping on the proxy to avoid fragmentation.
- Routing: Static routes are simpler for small deployments; BGP is supported and recommended for large-scale sites for automated failover. If you pick BGP, configure a low BFD interval for faster detection (we recommend 300ms +/-).
- Observability: you should expect per-connection metrics (rps, p50/p95 latency, kv cache hit-rate) emitted to a Prometheus-compatible endpoint and mirrored into your telemetry via our forwarder.

Prep items for the call:
- Your preferred pattern (dedicated proxy vs sidecar),
- A short list of subnets/IPs we can use for control-plane cidr allowlist,
- Any egress inspection (TLS interception) policies that might affect mTLS.

Attaching quick checklist and will paste the runbook link in the calendar invite.

Best,

Quick technical addendum (joining from infra):

Damian — a few specific recommendations based on what I see in the diagram:
1) Control-plane exposure
   - Ports: 443 (API), 8443 (internal admin) — only necessary source ports from your management CIDR.
   - TLS: Mutual TLS required for control-plane agent registration; we rotate certs quarterly by default.
2) Data-plane topology
   - If you run a dedicated proxy VM in your VPC, configure SNAT to preserve source where you need client IPs; otherwise our telemetry will see proxy IPs.
   - Sidecar pattern has the lowest tail latency but increases local IP churn; use an IPAM reservation scheme for predictable logs.
3) Routing and HA
   - For BGP: announce a /28 local, keep BGP communities simple. Use ECMP for multi-path; we accept ECMP equal-cost routes. Configure graceful restart and set BFD to 250ms for detection.
   - For static: implement health-check probes and an active/standby failover with a VIP to avoid traffic blackholes.
4) MTU & fragmentation
   - If your fabric is jumbo (9000), ensure any GRE/VxLAN overlay to our peers supports 9000; else MSS clamp at 1400-1420 on the proxy.
5) Conntrack and kernel tuning
   - If you expect >50k concurrent connections, bump conntrack max and tune hashsize; we can provide recommended sysctl settings.
6) Security & certs
   - We support a single mTLS trust bundle per-attachment. If you need distinct per-tenant bundles, that’s possible but adds rotation complexity.

Can prepare a short ops-runbook snippet for the call — I’ll attach a candidate snippet to the calendar. Also linking the acceptance checklist for network teams: https://redwood-inference.atlassian.net/browse/NET-1423

— Jonas
Infrastructure Architect | Redwood Inference
